advisories.description: Standing advisories raised during this sync (e.g. delivered changes touching a materialized input). Empty, not absent, when there are none — a consumer branches on length rather than presence.

complete.description: True iff the op ran its last phase and cleared its op-state, so nothing remains to `--continue` or `rwv abort`; false when a phase stopped it with its op-state held. A complete op exits 1 when `members` carries a `prune-refused` entry.

members.description: What replay did with each member checkout its per-repo outcomes do not cover: kept, pruned, or a prune that was refused. Empty, not absent, when there are none. A `prune-refused` entry is a checkout left on disk that no manifest names; branch on it. The op still completes, and then exits 1.

outcomes.description: One record per repo, sorted by repo path whatever `-j` is.

placements.description: How the files of each checkout the sync created or moved were placed. Empty, not absent, when it placed none.

refused.description: Each repo the op judged when it refused, with that state's choices. Empty, not absent, when it refused on none.

resolution.description: Resolved workspace coordinates (weave root, optional workweave identity, project). Absent when no project is resolved.

AdvisoryKindOutput.description: Closed vocabulary for [`AdvisoryOutput::kind`]. Adding a member is additive — existing consumers keep matching the members they know.

oneOf.description: Generated ecosystem state may no longer agree with the inputs it was derived from.

AdvisoryOutput.description:
A condition worth an operator's attention that a verb's `--json` output reports alongside its result, without being a failure of the verb itself.

Every field is something a consumer branches on directly — `kind` a closed enum, `remedy` a verb string runnable in the checkout where the advisory appears, `inputs` the workspace-relative paths that raised it. None of the three is a sentence a consumer would have to parse to act on.

Shared across verbs so more than one `--json` surface can emit the same vocabulary: a sync-time note and a doctor-time standing finding both fit this shape without either owning it.

inputs.description: Workspace-relative paths whose state raised this advisory.

remedy.description: The verb that resolves the advisory (e.g. `"rwv materialize"`).

Axis.description: What a refusal judged a repo on. Its token is the kind `rwv explain` serves; the order here is the order a repo's lines print in.

oneOf.description: Uncommitted work, or a VCS operation in progress, in a checkout.
Another checkout derives from what the verb would remove.
A branch and the branch it takes in from or publishes to.
A name the verb was given is unusable.
What `rwv push` withheld.
A project whose `rwv.toml` does not load.
The commit a lock pins for a member, and whether a ref reaches it.
A weave branch's record: how it is used and the branch it lands into.
How a branch accepts landings and takes its target's work in.
Projects sharing a member that record different `history` for it.
Where a workspace's checkouts sit against where the checked-out branch's record says they should.
A project's workweave index at the path earlier releases kept it at.
A branch rwv never rewrites, renames or deletes.
A project repo whose lock merge driver is not set up as this release sets it up.
A project commit `rwv cherry-pick` cannot port as it stands.

id.description: The choice's id on the axis's page; null for one it does not number.

run.description: The commands, one per line, as the terminal prints them.

where.description: The directory it must run in; null where it runs here or names its own directory.

ConflictOp.description:
In-flight VCS operation whose conflict needs human resolution.

Passed to [`Vcs::conflict_resolution_hint`] so sync's conflict-bail messages embed VCS-appropriate "how do I resume this?" text without hardcoding git vocabulary.

[`Vcs::mid_op`] constructs any variant from a repo's on-disk state, but a given field can be narrower than the type: every [`VcsError::RebaseConflict`] raised carries `Rebase`, so `Rebase` is the only value that field will actually carry.

oneOf.description:
Native rebase (`git rebase`).

The operator-facing resume path is `rwv sync --continue` / `rwv land --continue` — not bare `git rebase --continue`. The VCS hint for this variant stops at staging (`git add <files>`); rwv core appends the `rwv <verb> --continue` line. Bare `git rebase --continue` resumes without rwv's hold on the lock merge driver, so the clone's own definition merges the lock of each remaining pick.
Merge (`git merge`) — resumes with `git merge --continue`.
Cherry-pick (`git cherry-pick`) — resumes with `git cherry-pick --continue`. Used by sync's project-repo rebase-with-lock-exclusion path.
Revert (`git revert`) — resumes with `git revert --continue`.

ContainmentOutput.description:
What one repo's replay was decided from: how this checkout stood against the source, and which read of the source it was measured against.

The two travel together because a verdict without its baseline counts commits ahead of nothing in particular.

baseline.description: Which read produced the source tip this verdict measured against.

verdict.description: The ancestry between this checkout and the source tip.

ContainmentVerdictOutput.description: How a repo's checkout stood against the source tip it was measured against: equal to it, containing it and carrying commits it does not, contained by it, or each holding commits the other lacks.

FactKind.description: A fact about a judged repo. Facts are reported; they never select a choice.

oneOf.description: A superseded tip was recorded for the branch.
The branch is an ancestor of where it lands.
Another project's live lock pins the commits.
Other live weave branches declare the branch.
The pin is on the branch it lands into.
The member was left detached because its branch is checked out elsewhere.
The unlanded commits carry changes equivalent to commits where they land.

FilePlacement.description: How a member's tracked files reached a workspace.

hardlinked.description: Linked to another workspace's read-only copy.

reflinked.description: Cloned from another workspace's copy, sharing its storage until either is written.

written.description: Written by the version control system.

JudgedOutput.description: One judged repo, as `--json` carries it.

axis.description: What it was judged on; `rwv explain <axis>` serves the axis's page.

choices.description: What this state can run, in the order the page lists it.

listed.description: The files, paths or commits the state lists.

path.description: The repo's path, `projects/<name>` for the project repo.

state.description: The state it was judged in, as that page names it.

subject.description: What the state names, when it names something.

workspace.description: The workspace the repo was judged in, when that is not the one the verb ran in.

MemberOutput.description: What replay did with a member checkout outside its per-repo strategy: the member set the replayed manifest decides.

oneOf.description: The source's lock does not name this member and the manifest replay produced does, so its checkout stays.
The replayed manifest no longer names this member, and its checkout was removed.

The replayed manifest no longer names this member, but removing its checkout was refused. The checkout is still on disk, and once the op relocks no manifest or lock names it. The op runs to completion and then exits 1.

message.description: Free-form display message, the full cause chain. Not a typed discriminant.

refusal.description: The refusal token, resolvable with `rwv explain <token>`, when the removal was refused on a condition. Absent when it was refused on the checkout's state, which `refused` then carries, or failed without a classified refusal.

refused.description: Each state the checkout was judged in that refused the removal, with that state's choices; `rwv explain <axis>` serves each axis. Empty, not absent, when none was.

oneOf.description: The source's lock names this member and no checkout of it is on disk here, but creating one failed. It gets no per-repo outcome, and the op parks.

message.description: Free-form display message, the full cause chain. Not a typed discriminant.

refusal.description: The refusal token, resolvable with `rwv explain <token>`. Absent when the failure carries no classified refusal.

MidOperation.description: The operation a repository is stopped in: a conflict being resolved, or a bisect.

PlacementOutput.description: How the files of one checkout were placed when a verb created or moved it.

absolute_path.description: The checkout whose files were placed.

files.description: How many files were cloned, linked or written.

ReplayBaseline.description: Which read gave replay this repo's target.

Resolution.description:
Resolved workspace coordinates for `--json` output and the plugin env-var envelope.

Carries `workspace` (primary root abs path), `workweave` (the `<project>--<name>` identity the registry records), `project` (resolved project name), and `workweave_unregistered`. No `kind` or `location` field: the checkout is one of three states, and two of them are already carried by `workweave`'s presence.

The third state needs a field of its own. A workweave whose directory no registry entry names has no identity, so `workweave` is absent for it — and absent is what the primary looks like. Without `workweave_unregistered` the two serialize identically, and a consumer reading the documented meaning of that absence is told, positively, that it is at the primary checkout.

Results only — provenance (which chain step resolved the project, which flag addressed the workspace) is deliberately excluded: anything in default `--json` output becomes depended on, and the assertion use case needs the result, not the mechanism. Provenance appears only in the human-facing "target:" line printed to stderr.

Isomorphic to the plugin env-var envelope (`RWV_WORKSPACE`/`RWV_WORKWEAVE`/`RWV_WORKWEAVE_UNREGISTERED`/`RWV_PROJECT`): both surfaces are pure projections of [`WorkspaceContext::resolution`], never independently computed.

project.description: Resolved project name; absent when the workspace resolved but no project did (a primary with no project selected).

workweave.description:
Workweave identity (`<project>--<name>`), as the primary-side registry records it.

Absent at the primary, and absent for a workweave whose directory no registry entry names — identity is by record, so an unregistered workweave has no identity to report and rwv will not spell one from the directory name. Those two absences are told apart by `workweave_unregistered`, not by this field.

workweave_unregistered.description:
`true` when the invocation resolved into a workweave whose directory no registry entry names, so `workweave` above is absent for a reason that is not "this is the primary".

Serialized only in that state, so the primary and a registered workweave emit exactly the bytes they emitted before this field existed. `rwv doctor --fix` registers such a directory, after which this is absent and `workweave` carries the identity.

Step3AdvanceOutput.description:
Step-3 fast-forward advance record for one repo in `rwv land --json` output.

Present in a per-repo outcome iff step 3 (advance-target) actually advanced that repo's branch pointer, and carrying the revisions that advance read and wrote. Omitted (`skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`) on a no-op advance — the target was already at CWD's tip — which is the same condition under which the text line reads `already at <sha>`, because both render one outcome.

from_sha.description: Target repo's HEAD SHA before the fast-forward.

to_sha.description: Target repo's HEAD SHA after the fast-forward (== CWD's tip).

SyncFailureOutput.description:
Wire-output mirror of [`SyncFailure`] for `--json` emission.

Carries the same payload as the in-memory enum but with a `cause` represented as the serializable [`VcsErrorOutput`].

`message` is the human-readable display string of the failure (free-form text, not a typed discriminant). `cause` is the structured typed cause — always present on `ff-impossible` and `rebase-failed`, optional on `head-unreadable` — and consumers that want to branch on failure mode should inspect `cause.kind` rather than parsing `message`.

message.description: Free-form display message for this failure. Not a typed discriminant.
Free-form display message for this failure. Not a typed discriminant.
Free-form display message for this failure. Not a typed discriminant.

SyncOutcomeOutput.description: One per-repo record in `rwv sync --json` output.

containment.description: How this checkout stood against the source when the strategy ran. The `kind` says what the strategy did; this says what it was up against — `behind` is a fast-forward, `diverged` is a rebase.

derived_content_dropped.description: Repo-relative paths this repo declares derived whose replayed version the landed tree does not carry: the replay resolved them to the target's version instead. Regenerating them from their source of record and committing is what makes the landed tree describe itself again. Omitted when nothing was resolved away.

step3_advance.description: Step-3 fast-forward advance for this repo; present only in `rwv land --json` output when step 3 advanced this repo.

containment.description: How this checkout stood against the source, and which read of the source `commits_ahead` counts against.

source_position.description: Where the SOURCE's own checkout stood against that same read of the source. `containment` proves this repo holds the target; only this says whether the source has since moved past it. Absent where the source's checkout could not be measured.

step3_advance.description: Step-3 fast-forward advance for this repo; present only in `rwv land --json` output when step 3 advanced this repo.

containment.description: How this checkout stood against the source, and which read of the source it was equal to.

step3_advance.description: Step-3 fast-forward advance for this repo; present only in `rwv land --json` output when step 3 advanced this repo.

containment.description: How this checkout stood against the source when the strategy ran. `failure.message` renders this in prose; branch on this instead. Absent where the outcome was decided before any pair was read.

step3_advance.description: Step-3 fast-forward advance for this repo; present only in `rwv land --json` output when step 3 advanced this repo. Typically absent when the repo failed in step 1.

VcsErrorOutput.description:
Wire-output mirror of [`VcsError`] for `--json` emission.

`VcsError` itself can't derive `Serialize` cleanly because tuple variants (and `io::Error`) don't play nicely with serde's internally-tagged enum representation. This struct-only mirror does: every variant carries named fields, and a `From<&VcsError>` impl converts at JSON-emission time.

message.description: Display form of the underlying `io::Error`. The native source is dropped at the wire boundary since `io::Error` does not serialize. Named `message` (not `error`) to make clear this is free-form display text, not a typed discriminant that consumers can branch on.
